definitions.explanation: The geological process of land rising or being pushed upward, or the resulting elevated landform.
A raised area on a surface, including on the body. Used in medical and general descriptive contexts.

examples.japanese: {地殻|ちかく}の{隆起|りゅうき}によって{山|やま}が{形成|けいせい}された。
examples.english: Mountains were formed by the uplift of the earth's crust.

examples.japanese: この{海岸|かいがん}は{隆起|りゅうき}サンゴ{礁|しょう}でできている。
examples.english: This coastline is made of uplifted coral reef.

examples.japanese: {能登半島|のとはんとう}{地震|じしん}では{海底|かいてい}が{隆起|りゅうき}し、{海岸線|かいがんせん}が{大|おお}きく{変化|へんか}した。
examples.english: In the Noto Peninsula earthquake, the seabed was uplifted, dramatically changing the coastline.

examples.japanese: {皮膚|ひふ}に{小|ちい}さな{隆起|りゅうき}がある。
examples.english: There is a small bump on the skin.

examples.japanese: {骨|ほね}の{隆起|りゅうき}{部分|ぶぶん}を{触|さわ}ると{痛|いた}い。
examples.english: It hurts when I touch the protruding part of the bone.

examples.japanese: {地面|じめん}の{隆起|りゅうき}のせいで{道路|どうろ}にひびが{入|はい}っている。
examples.english: The road has cracks due to the ground swelling up.

notes:
A compound of {隆|りゅう} (to rise; prominent) and {起|き} (to rise; to occur). Most commonly encountered in geology and earth science, but also used in medicine and anatomy. Japan's volcanic and seismic geography makes this a relatively common word in news reporting.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {隆起|りゅうき}する: to be uplifted; to rise; to swell
- {地殻|ちかく}{隆起|りゅうき}: crustal uplift
- {隆起|りゅうき}サンゴ{礁|しょう}: uplifted coral reef
- {海底|かいてい}の{隆起|りゅうき}: seabed uplift
- {隆起|りゅうき}{部|ぶ}: protuberance; raised area

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {沈降|ちんこう}: subsidence — the opposite process; land sinking down
- {膨|ふく}らみ: swelling; bulge — a softer, everyday term for something that puffs up
- {突起|とっき}: protrusion; projection — a sharp or pointed raised part
